scene: Established same-identity B surface may be a new face of an unchanged object or a relocated object. Off-share alone cannot identify these with arbitrary certainty.
model: README M1h: geometry soft Bernoulli composite likelihood for latent off fraction theta; same-state/view-selection reference includes theta in[0,1], moved hypothesis restricts theta>1/2. Symmetric Jeffreys reference prior gives restriction mass1/2 and BF=2*Beta posterior tail(theta>1/2). Combine once with q for movement odds; preserve P05 coverage eligibility separately.
correlation: Use actual original copy vertex weights grouped at existing r. Perfect within-cell correlation and independence between cells gives Kish effective spatial count N^2/sum_c N_c^2; original soft off mean unchanged. This is variance-matched fractional likelihood, not exact independent-binomial data. Do not multiply reliable-count n by mesh fraction.
no_tuning: Original r andT, original majority boundary1/2; Jeffreys halves already model reference choice; BF2 from symmetric truncation mass. No fitted slopes/cutoffs/extra constants. One prospective trial, original tests unchanged.
preservation_mechanism: With sufficient spatial evidence near-majority support gives small tail, keeping same-site copies. Majority-off increases movement odds only finitely because different-face views remain possible. q <=1/3 cannot be retired by this ambiguous geometry alone, a consequence of BF<=2; old-site measured absence and history remain available elsewhere. No category-table Boolean gate here.
limitations: New view and moved hypotheses overlap observationally; finite BF is intentional model structure, not claimed learned/calibrated from GT.
Spatial-cell independence and fractional-count likelihood are approximations; actual fixed tests and datasets determine retention.
P05 established decision and P08-P11 consumption sites remain as previously accepted; this is not whole-algorithm completion.
